name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (16 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found as of 16 Nov; Mayon at alert level 3
state: Philippine authorities raised Mayon's alert level from 2 to 3 on 30 Oct after an eruption sent ash about 3,000 metres high; pilots were told to avoid the summit, but no flight disruption was reported (The Star). Searches on 16 Nov found no red aviation colour code at a volcano near major air routes, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure. Ongoing eruptions remain local hazards, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Air travellers in Indonesia and the Philippines can see short-notice delays when ash advisories are issued. People living near active volcanoes should follow local observatory and civil protection guidance.
rubric_hit: No aviation colour code red, no large eruption: Normal

sources.title: The Star — Philippines raises volcano alert level as blast sends ash skyward

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
